title: Rollback Strategies and Health Probes
description: Get back to a known-good state in minutes when a release goes wrong, including schema changes.

data.text: Twenty minutes after a release, error rate climbs to 12%. The team's documented rollback procedure is "redeploy the previous commit", which takes 25 minutes to build and deploy — longer than the incident has already lasted, and it rebuilds from source rather than restoring the exact artifact that was running.

Make rollback a **routing decision, not a build**. Keep the previous artifact intact in the staging slot and rollback becomes swapping the slots back — seconds, no build. Ensure health probes mark an unhealthy instance out of rotation automatically so a degraded release sheds traffic before a human notices. For database rollback, rely on the **expand/contract** discipline: the previous app version is still schema-compatible, so no reversal is needed.

data.title: One-command rollback
data.code:
# Previous version is still running in the staging slot — swap back
az webapp deployment slot swap \
  --resource-group rg-quotient-prod \
  --name app-quotient-prod \
  --slot staging \
  --target-slot production

# For a canary: just send all traffic back to stable
az afd origin update \
  --resource-group rg-quotient-prod \
  --profile-name afd-quotient \
  --origin-group-name checkout-origins \
  --origin-name canary \
  --weight 0
az afd origin update \
  --resource-group rg-quotient-prod \
  --profile-name afd-quotient \
  --origin-group-name checkout-origins \
  --origin-name stable \
  --weight 1000

data.title: Probe configuration that sheds a bad instance
data.code:
# In the App Service site config
healthCheckPath: /health/ready        # instances failing this leave rotation

# Front Door / App Gateway probe
probePath: /health/ready
probeProtocol: Https
probeIntervalInSeconds: 30
numberOfProbesToUnhealthy: 3          # ~90s to eject a bad instance

data.text: Also keep a **small feature flag** for the riskiest part of each release. Rolling back a flag takes one second and requires no deployment at all, which is often faster than any routing change.

During an incident, every minute of rolling back is a minute of impact. A rebuild pipeline is the worst possible rollback mechanism because it is slow, non-deterministic (dependency versions may have moved), and competes for the same build agents that are also trying to produce a fix.

cards.title: Slot swap back
cards.description: Previous version still warm in staging
cons: Only one version of history retained by default

cards.title: Canary weight to zero
cards.description: Return all traffic to stable origin
cons: Requires Front Door or App Gateway tier
Does not help if stable origin was replaced

cards.title: Rebuild and redeploy previous commit
cons: Uses build infrastructure needed for the fix
